clue.text: One unfinished poem absorbed by 9's sister in place of learning

indicators.note: something absorbed by another is taken into it, so the first pieces go inside the sister's name

parts.note: 9 is Nancy Mitford, whose sister was Unity Mitford
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: a poem left unfinished loses its final letter

parts.note: a verse is a poem

explanation.surface: A half-written poem is soaked up by a famous writer's sister somewhere studious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts VERSE to VERS; with I (one) it goes inside UNITY, Nancy Mitford's sister, splitting her name into UN...ITY.
explanation.definitionFit: A university is an institution of higher education, a seat of scholarship.

clue.text: Unorthodoxly made turn not previously envisaged

indicators.note: done in an unorthodox way, so the letters of the following words are taken in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone turned in an odd way that nobody expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unorthodoxly' rearranges the eight letters of MADE TURN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something never even dreamed of was never imagined or foreseen.

clue.text: Drinks slowly, imbibing your sweet liquids

indicators.note: imbibing means taking in, so the drinking word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls

explanation.surface: Someone sips their sugary drinks at leisure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imbibing' puts YR (your) inside SUPS, between S and UPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Syrups are thick sugary solutions, sweet fluids poured on food.

clue.text: Annoyed bishop, say, in bar

parts.note: cross means annoyed
a bishop is an example of a chess piece

explanation.surface: An irritated churchman is found in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes the bishop a clergyman and the bar a pub; he is a chessman and the bar is a beam.
explanation.definitionFit: A crosspiece is a beam or rod laid across a structure, a transverse rail.

clue.text: Heartless marriage shown up as beyond the pale

indicators.note: in a down entry, shown up means the letters are read upwards, from bottom to top
heartless means the middle letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a union is a marriage

explanation.surface: A loveless wedding is exposed as utterly unacceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' takes the middle I from UNION, giving UNON; 'shown up' reads it upwards as NONU. Non-U, in Nancy Mitford's terms, means not upper-class.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-U was the label for speech or manners not acceptable among the upper classes, i.e. socially out of bounds.

clue.text: They remove paint, for example, ruining press car

indicators.note: ruining wrecks the words, so their letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Tools that strip paint are wrecking a car in a press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruining' rearranges the eight letters of PRESS CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapers are hand tools with flat blades for stripping off coatings such as old paint.

clue.text: Under Menelaus, initially, very small rebellion

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of these names and words

parts.note: tiny means very small

explanation.surface: A tiny uprising takes place under King Menelaus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives M and U; in this down entry the U of Under sits under the M of Menelaus, then TINY follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutiny is a revolt, especially by sailors or soldiers against their officers.

clue.text: Plant very fine specimen outside!

indicators.note: outside means the specimen word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: a gem is a prize specimen, the best of its kind
U, Nancy Mitford's label for upper-class usage, marks what is very fine or refined

explanation.surface: Someone admires a wonderful plant growing outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle's theme is U and non-U; here U stands for the refined. GEM wraps around it, giving GE...M.
explanation.definitionFit: Geum is a genus of flowering herbs in the rose family, also called avens.

clue.text: English writer in French city with college president

parts.note: Nancy is a city in Lorraine, France
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
Gerald Ford was a US president

explanation.surface: An English author is living in a French city alongside a college president.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface places the writer in France with an academic; the city, college and president are simply joined end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: Nancy Mitford was an English novelist, author of The Pursuit of Love, who popularised U and non-U.

clue.text: Change to a course for reason that's basic

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters that follow

explanation.surface: Someone changes course for a fundamental reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' rearranges the nine letters of TO A COURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A root cause is the fundamental origin of a problem, its underlying explanation.

clue.text: Strive somehow to include universal qualities that are good

indicators.note: to include means the rearranged letters take the other piece inside them
somehow suggests the letters are put together in some new order

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for universal, as in film certificates

explanation.surface: Somehow we strive to be good in every way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges STRIVE to VIRTES; 'to include' puts U (universal) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtues are moral excellences, admirable traits of character.

clue.text: Metal briefly found in front of VW

definitions.text: Metal briefly found in front of VW

parts.words: Metal briefly found in front of VW
parts.note: this metal, given briefly as its chemical symbol, is the letter that comes just before V and W in the alphabet

explanation.surface: A piece of metal turns up on the front of a Volkswagen.
explanation.walkthrough: VW looks like the car maker, but it is the letters V and W; the metal's symbol, U, precedes them in the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Uranium is a heavy radioactive metallic element with chemical symbol U.

clue.text: Wrongly taking rap, user shows indignation

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters are put in the wrong order and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A drug user, wrongly blamed, gets angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrongly' rearranges the seven letters of RAP USER; 'taking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear up is to react angrily or defiantly, like a horse rising on its hind legs.

clue.text: 15, 20, and 22, say, in practice

indicators.note: say tells us to listen to how the named entries sound when spoken

parts.note: these entries all sound like the letter U, so together they are Us

explanation.surface: A list of items is offered as examples in practice.
explanation.walkthrough: Entries 15, 20 and 22 are all pronounced like the letter U; said together they are 'U's', which sounds like USE.
explanation.definitionFit: Use is habitual practice or custom, as in 'in common use'.

clue.text: 16 with rich person, provided it's not seen

parts.note: 16 is upper class, abbreviated as U
a nob is a wealthy or upper-class person
served means provided, as food is

explanation.surface: An upper-class group dines with a wealthy man, as long as nobody notices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided' looks like 'on condition that', but it means SERVED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unobserved has gone unnoticed by anyone watching.

clue.text: Person doing this puzzle, not altogether joyously

indicators.note: not altogether means only a part of the word is used, a run inside it

explanation.surface: The solver is working on the crossword, but without full delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not altogether' points to a run inside JOYOUSLY.
explanation.definitionFit: The solver is addressed directly as the second person, the reader of the clue.

clue.text: Part of Oxford lesson for privileged group

parts.note: an Oxford is a style of shoe, and the upper is part of a shoe
a class is a lesson

explanation.surface: Part of a lesson at Oxford University is for the elite.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford looks like the university, but it is a lace-up shoe, whose upper part sits above the sole.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper class is the aristocratic or wealthiest social stratum.

clue.text: In suggestion about rapacious doctor providing help for patient

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the suggestion word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a tip is a suggestion
ravenous means greedy, like rapacious

explanation.surface: In a hint, a greedy doctor is giving help to a sick person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts TIP around RAVENOUS and DR, after IN; 'providing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An intravenous drip feeds fluids or drugs into a patient's vein, a hospital aid.

clue.text: He's held up by a scumbag in old pub

indicators.note: held by means kept inside, so the letters go within the other pieces

parts.note: a louse is a contemptible person, a scumbag

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A man is held up by a villain in an old tavern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns HE to EH; 'held' puts it inside A LOUSE, after the L. 'He's held up' looks like a robbery but is two signals.
explanation.definitionFit: An alehouse is a dated word for a tavern serving beer.

clue.text: Like poor service, perhaps, not included

definitions.meaning: a bad tennis serve may be judged out, an umpire's call against it
excluded or rejected as a possibility

explanation.definitionFit: A fault serve is declared out by the umpire; separately, an option rejected has been excluded from consideration.

clue.text: What'll make very fine bow, ultimately

definitions.text: What'll make very fine bow, ultimately

parts.words: What'll make very fine bow, ultimately
parts.note: this tree's wood, once seasoned, makes the finest longbows; its name also sounds like U, the theme's mark of refinement

explanation.surface: Something will in the end produce an excellent bow.
explanation.walkthrough: English longbows were traditionally made of this tree's wood; 'very fine' nods to the theme of U (refined).
explanation.definitionFit: The yew is an evergreen tree whose springy wood was used for medieval longbows.

clue.text: Turkey has this material for making walls

definitions.meaning: the fleshy red lobe hanging from a turkey's throat
woven rods and twigs plastered with daub to build walls

explanation.definitionFit: A wattle is the fleshy flap under a bird's throat; separately, interlaced stakes form the framework of wattle-and-daub walls.

clue.text: Animal's initial direction followed by 24

parts.note: E for east, the direction faced at the start
24 is U-turns: from east one U-turn faces west, a second faces east again

explanation.surface: An animal starts off one way and then follows another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Facing E, one U-turn points W and a second points E again, so 24 supplies W then E.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewe is a female sheep, a farm animal.

clue.text: Single person having a row — kitchen's not finished

indicators.note: not finished means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a scullery is a back kitchen for washing up

explanation.surface: A lone person is quarrelling, and the kitchen is left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel but is rowing a boat; 'not finished' drops the last Y of SCULLERY.
explanation.definitionFit: A sculler rows a boat alone using a pair of oars.

clue.text: Complete reversals in 12 attacks

parts.note: 12 is uranium, whose chemical symbol is U
turns are attacks, as in fits of illness

explanation.surface: Total about-faces happen in a dozen assaults.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is not a number but entry 12, uranium, symbol U; turns as attacks means fits or bouts.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-turn is a turnaround, an abrupt change to the opposite direction or policy.

clue.text: See 9
As way to keep hands warm, a failure

definitions.meaning: a fur tube into which both hands are tucked
a bungle or botch, a fumbled attempt

explanation.definitionFit: A muff is a tubular hand-warmer; separately, a botched catch or attempt is a fumble.

clue.text: 16 in parties, in pairs

indicators.note: in means the upper-class letter is placed inside the parties word

parts.note: dos are parties, as in 'a big do'
16 is upper class, abbreviated as U

explanation.surface: Toffs go to parties in couples.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' puts U inside DOS; the second is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Duos are pairs of performers or people, couples.

clue.text: Circular letter in form of verse

definitions.meaning: a round figure, such as a ring-shaped character or disc
a short poem with refrains, a variant of the rondeau

explanation.definitionFit: A roundel is a small disc or ring-shaped emblem, here a round letter like O; separately, it is a poem type with a refrain.

clue.text: Notes for all the players showing final result

definitions.meaning: a musical score showing every instrument's part
the complete result at the end of a match

explanation.definitionFit: A full score sets out the music for every instrument in an orchestra; separately, it is the end result of a game.

clue.text: Intelligence about new parts of speech

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the intelligence word goes round the other letter

parts.note: nous is common sense or intelligence

explanation.surface: Someone shows intelligence about new ways of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts N inside NOUS, after NOU.
explanation.definitionFit: Nouns are naming words, one of the grammatical word classes.
